Overview 
The June 2026 Quarter marked a significant step forward for Lac Gold Limited (“Lac Gold” or “the 
Company”), with completion of Stage 1 drilling, commencement of Stage 2 drilling and exceptional 
drilling results materially strengthening the Company's understanding of the Rouyn Gold Project in 
Québec, Canada. 
Drilling at the Astoria deposit continued to demonstrate a large structurally controlled gold system 
comprising broad mineralised envelopes containing multiple higher-grade shoots. The results received 
during the Quarter indicate that high-grade mineralisation is more continuous and extensive than 
previously interpreted and modelled, increasing confidence in the evolving geological model and the 
potential for future resource growth. 
The Company completed its initial approximately 15,000-metre Stage 1 drilling program and 
transitioned directly into an additional 15,000-metre (Stage 2) program before Quarter end. Technical, 
environmental and stakeholder workstreams continued in parallel as Lac Gold systematically 
advances the geological understanding and development evaluation of Rouyn. 
During the Quarter, Lac Gold also completed the acquisition of the historic Golden Patricia Gold Mine 
and surrounding property from Barrick. Golden Patricia produced 619,796 ounces of gold at an average 
grade of 16.48g/t between 1988-1997†. Golden Patricia consolidates the Company's position in the 
Pickle Lake district and provides a second long-term growth platform. Rouyn remains Lac Gold's 
flagship asset, primary value driver and immediate focus for management attention and capital 
allocation. 
The Company's strategy is straightforward: grow and advance Rouyn; systematically assess and 
unlock value within Pickle Lake; and allocate capital and management attention to the 
opportunities offering the greatest potential for shareholder value creation.

Rouyn Gold Project (Québec, Canada) 
Project context 
The Rouyn Gold Project is located immediately south of Rouyn-Noranda, within the Abitibi Greenstone 
Belt of Québec. The project lies along the Cadillac–Larder Lake Break, a major regional structure 
associated with numerous world-class gold deposits and mining operations. 
Rouyn hosts a Mineral Resource Estimate of 15.8Mt at 3.28g/t Au for 1.66Moz of gold (JORC 2012). The 
Mineral Resource extends across part of an approximately six-kilometre mineralised corridor and 
remains open along strike and at depth. 
Rouyn is a brownfields resource growth opportunity. The Company’s immediate objective is to improve 
confidence in the geological model, grow the gold inventory and create shareholder value through 
disciplined technical execution. 
 
Figure 2 – Abitibi region and Rouyn location plan 
Drilling program 
During the Quarter, Lac Gold completed its initial 15,000-metre Stage 1 diamond drilling program and 
immediately commenced a further 15,000-metre Stage 2 program. A second drill rig was mobilised in 
April 2026 to accelerate drilling across the Rouyn corridor. 
During the Quarter, 43 holes were completed for 16,212 metres. At 30 June 2026, 54 holes had been 
completed for 20,551 metres cumulatively under the 2026 drilling programs.

Stage 1 was designed to test the continuity and geometry of mineralisation, refine the geological model 
and assess extensions to the current Mineral Resource. Stage 2 continues this work and is focused on: 
• 
extending known mineralisation at Astoria, including higher-grade zones along strike and down-
plunge; 
• 
testing down-dip continuity between approximately 400m and 1,000m depth; and 
• 
advancing additional targets along the Cadillac–Larder Lake Break corridor with the objective 
of expanding and linking known gold occurrences. 
Drilling results and geological interpretation 
Assay results announced on 4 June and 30 June 2026 continued to demonstrate higher-grade gold 
shoots within broad mineralised envelopes at Astoria. These results strengthened the Company's 
interpretation that mineralisation is more continuous and extensive than previously modelled.

continuity of the mineralised system. 
The geological information collected during Stage 1 supports an interpretation of Astoria as a large, 
structurally controlled orogenic gold system. Broad shear-hosted hydrothermal alteration envelopes 
contain multiple higher-grade shoots associated with secondary and tertiary structures. The growing 
body of drilling information—not any single intercept—is improving confidence in the geological model 
and supporting the assessment of future resource growth opportunities.

Technical and development workstreams 
Technical workstreams progressed in parallel with drilling to support the disciplined evaluation of 
potential development pathways for Rouyn. 
• 
Geological modelling and interpretation continued as new drilling, logging and assay 
information became available. 
• 
The project gap analysis was completed, identifying the principal technical work required to 
advance project evaluation. 
• 
Metallurgical optimisation work advanced, including planning for additional test work on 
mineralisation types not fully represented in the existing metallurgical dataset. 
• 
Preliminary mining, infrastructure and economic workstreams continued to inform the scope 
and sequencing of future studies. 
The Company will continue to integrate new geological information before determining the timing and 
scope of the next formal Mineral Resource update and subsequent development studies.

Environment, permitting and community engagement 
Lac Gold continued to progress environmental, permitting and stakeholder workstreams during the 
Quarter. Activities included advancement of the environmental baseline program, ongoing permitting 
work and structured engagement with local stakeholders. 
The first meeting of the Rouyn Project monitoring committee (Comité de suivi) was held in April 2026. 
The committee provides a structured forum for dialogue with community representatives and supports 
the Company's commitment to transparent and responsible project advancement. 
The Company continued engagement with the City of Rouyn-Noranda, local residents and the 
Abitibiwinni First Nation. Operational measures continued to be reviewed and adjusted where 
appropriate in response to local conditions and stakeholder feedback.

PICKLE LAKE GOLD PROJECT (ONTARIO, CANADA) 
Golden Patricia acquisition 
On 9 June 2026, Lac Gold announced completion of the acquisition of the historic high-grade Golden 
Patricia Gold Mine and surrounding property from a subsidiary of Barrick Mining Corporation. 
Golden Patricia historically produced approximately 619,796 ounces of gold at an average grade of 
16.48g/t Au and an average recovery of 96.1% between 1988 and 1997. The acquisition consolidates 
Lac Gold's landholding in the Pickle Lake district, adds a significant past-producing gold centre and 
provides access to an extensive historical exploration and mining dataset. 
The acquisition was completed on the previously announced non-cash terms, including a 2% net 
smelter return royalty in favour of Barrick and assumption of agreed environmental obligations.

Data compilation and evaluation 
The immediate priority for Golden Patricia is to evaluate the extensive historical information. The 
Company commenced planning for digitisation, indexing and integration of historical exploration and 
mining records during the Quarter. 
The planned work program includes: 
• 
digitisation and validation of historical drilling, geological, mining and production information; 
• 
integration of the datasets into a modern project database; 
• 
development and refinement of geological interpretations; and 
• 
generation and prioritisation of future exploration targets. 
No material field exploration was undertaken at Pickle Lake during the Quarter. Pickle Lake and Golden 
Patricia provide a second growth platform and long-term strategic optionality that complements rather 
than competes with Rouyn.

Change of Company name 
At a general meeting held on 21 May 2026, shareholders approved the change of the Company's name 
from Ardiden Limited to Lac Gold Limited. The name change reflects the Company's strategy of building 
a long-term Canadian gold company, with Rouyn as its flagship asset and Pickle Lake providing an 
additional growth platform. 
The Company's ASX code changed from ADV to LAC following implementation of the name change.

Payments to related parties totalled A$342k, comprising directors' fees, salaries and associated costs. 
Further details are provided in the accompanying Appendix 5B.

The Company had 214,906,395 fully paid ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026. There was no change

STRATEGY AND OUTLOOK 
Rouyn remains Lac Gold's flagship asset and primary value driver. The Company's immediate focus is 
to continue drilling, assess the potential to grow the existing 1.66Moz Mineral Resource and advance 
the technical and environmental work required to evaluate future development pathways. 
Key priorities for the September 2026 Quarter include: 
• 
receipt and interpretation of remaining Stage 1 assay results; 
• 
continued Stage 2 drilling and assay results; 
• 
refinement of the Astoria geological model and assessment of resource growth opportunities; 
• 
advancement of metallurgical optimisation, environmental baseline and development 
workstreams; 
• 
continued permitting and stakeholder engagement at Rouyn; and 
• 
digitisation and integration of the Golden Patricia historical dataset. 
Recent drilling and geological interpretation have materially strengthened the Company's confidence 
that Rouyn has the potential to become significantly larger than previously understood. Pickle Lake and 
Golden Patricia provide additional long-term strategic optionality, while management's immediate 
focus remains firmly on advancing and growing Rouyn.

About Lac Gold Limited 
Lac Gold Limited is a Canadian-focused gold company advancing the Rouyn Gold Project in Québec 
and the Pickle Lake Gold Project in Ontario. 
The Rouyn Gold Project is located on the Cadillac Break within the Abitibi gold region and hosts a large 
existing Mineral Resource Estimate (refer ASX:ADV announcement dated 10 October 2025). 
The Pickle Lake Gold Project includes the historic Golden Patricia Mine and a district-scale landholding 
within the Uchi Geological Subprovince of Ontario. 
The Company is focused on disciplined project advancement through targeted exploration, technical 
evaluation, responsible development and strong local partnerships.
